// design-studio harness — generated, do not edit
//
// Generated by the OpenChamber Design Studio extension. Rewritten in place when a
// design session starts; any manual edit is lost on the next write. Change the
// rules in the extension (shared/harness-text.ts), not here.
//
// Side effects of this file living in the project:
//  · OpenCode discovers `.opencode/plugin/*.ts` and loads it into every session
//    for this project automatically.
//  · It imports only Node built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`), so it adds no
//    dependency and needs no `node_modules` install. If `.opencode/` is not
//    tracked, add it to `.gitignore`.
//
// What it does:
//  · Pushes the Design Studio harness rules into every model turn (identity,
//    design-system authority, craft rules, verification protocol, mandate).
//  · Flags the session after a completed edit/write/patch so the next turn
//    carries an explicit verification nudge.
//  · Moves a session that the extension has opted in (a per-session request
//    file under `.design-studio/isolate/`) into its own per-chat workspace at
//    `<project>/designs/<slug>`, creates that folder, and tells the agent to
//    scaffold the project there. Idempotent, and a no-op for every other
//    session and for any session already inside a `designs/` path.

import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"

const HARNESS_RULES = "You are an expert designer. HTML is your tool, not your medium: the medium is the intent, the system and the craft of the page.\n\n# Design Studio harness\nThis session is a Design Studio session. These rules are mandatory for every edit and every reply.\n\n## Design system authority\nDESIGN.md and tokens.css (when present) are the project design system and are authoritative: follow them over any conflicting instinct, and do not invent colours, spacing or type values outside them. A hardcoded value that a token already covers is a defect.\n\n## Craft rules\n### typography\n- Build one modular scale (base ×1.2, or ×1.25 for airier layouts) and take every size from it.\n- Ship 6–8 sizes total; do not invent a new size per section.\n- Pair a distinct display face with a readable body face, and keep each role to one family.\n- Set body line-height near 1.5 and tighten only display text.\n- Keep body measure to roughly 45–75 characters per line.\n- Let weight, size and color carry hierarchy before you reach for decoration.\n- Use tabular numerals for tables, prices, timers and any aligned data.\n- Limit to two or three weights per family; resist faux-bold.\n\n### color\n- Keep 70–90% of the palette neutral; let structure do the work.\n- Spend one accent on 5–10% of a screen, used at most twice as a fill or emphasis.\n- Reserve semantic colors (success/warn/danger/info) for 0–5% and only for meaning.\n- Guarantee contrast of 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and UI edges.\n- Never encode meaning in color alone; add an icon, label or weight change.\n- Derive surfaces from one neutral ramp rather than stacking unrelated grays.\n- Test the palette in both light and dark before committing.\n- Choose an accent that fits the direction; do not fall back to framework default.\n\n### anti-slop\n- Do not use the default indigo/violet accent that every starter kit ships.\n- Do not build hero sections from two-stop gradient backgrounds.\n- Do not use emoji as icons; draw or pick a coherent icon set.\n- Do not invent metrics, testimonials or logos the brief did not supply.\n- Do not pad copy with filler like \"lorem ipsum\" or \"seamless, powerful solution\".\n- Avoid the generic card with a colored left border and a shadow.\n- Avoid stock centered-everything layouts with no alignment logic.\n- If a pattern feels like a template default, redesign it deliberately.\n\n### states\n- Render every data surface in all five states: Loading, Empty, Error, Populated, Edge.\n- Give Loading a skeleton or spinner, and a fallback message after ~15s.\n- Make Empty states explain what belongs here and how to fill it.\n- Make Error states say what failed and offer the next action.\n- Cover Edge cases: one item, many items, very long strings, missing fields.\n- Give forms explicit Untouched, Dirty and Submitted-pending states.\n- Disable or show progress on submit, then confirm success or surface failure.\n- Validate on blur, not on every keystroke.\n\n### motion\n- Animate only to explain change, never as decoration.\n- Keep UI transitions under 300ms; longer motion needs a reason.\n- Make motion interruptible: a new input cancels the running one.\n- Honor prefers-reduced-motion and provide a static equivalent.\n- Move along a clear path; avoid bounce and overshoot on functional elements.\n- Stagger lists slightly, but never block reading on animation completion.\n\n### accessibility\n- Give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible treatment.\n- Label every input; a placeholder is not a label.\n- Provide a complete keyboard path, with no focus traps.\n- Use semantic elements first and ARIA only to fill the gaps.\n- Keep contrast at AA: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI.\n- Give images meaningful alt text, and decorative images an empty alt.\n- Announce dynamic updates through a live region.\n\n### laws-of-ux\n- Hick: cut the number of simultaneous choices; group or defer the rest.\n- Miller: keep working sets near 7±2, and lean toward ~4 for menus.\n- Fitts: make primary targets large and near where the pointer already is.\n- von Restorff: style the one thing that must stand out; mute the rest.\n- Peak-End: invest in the strongest moment and the final step.\n- Tesler: absorb complexity in the product so the user faces less of it.\n\n### responsive\n- Define named breakpoints (e.g. sm/md/lg/xl) and reuse them everywhere.\n- Reflow, do not merely shrink: change column counts and stacking per breakpoint.\n- Test the awkward widths, not just the presets: 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440.\n- Keep tap targets at least 44px on touch layouts.\n- Clamp fluid type and spacing so extremes stay legible.\n- Never let horizontal scroll appear on a normal content page.\n\n### verification\n- Never call a change done until you have seen it render at every breakpoint: mobile 390, desktop 1280, wide 2048.\n- Also check the awkward widths where relevant: 320, 375, 1024, 1440.\n- Horizontal scroll on a normal content page is a defect, not a style choice.\n- Fix the cheapest deterministic failure first; never restyle to hide an overflow or a contrast error.\n- Use only tokens from tokens.css / DESIGN.md; a hardcoded colour or spacing value is a defect.\n- Keep tap targets at least 24px (44px on touch), headings in order, every control labelled.\n- Done means the gates pass at every breakpoint — not that it looks right at one width.\n\n## Verification protocol\nBefore editing, state the change's acceptance criteria in one line.\nAfter each edit verify in this order (cheap/deterministic first): overflow → design tokens → accessibility → semantics → layout. Use the browser tool: `browser.capture` / `browser.open` returns a `verification` block covering every viewport (mobile, tablet, desktop, wide) with each gate's status.\nFix every P0 before starting a new gate tier; re-run the same gates after a fix.\nBudget: at most 5 fix/verify iterations OR 10 minutes, whichever comes first. Then stop and report.\nNever mark the work done while any P0 remains. Report the gate table and state the breakpoints you checked.\nOscillation: if a finding you already fixed reappears, or a gate flips across two iterations, STOP and hand back with both states. Do not keep looping.\nThe 0–10 critique is advisory only; never treat it as pass/fail and never optimise for it.\n\n## Mandate\nVerify at every stage, not only at the end: after each edit, before showing work, and before calling anything done. Run the cheap deterministic gates first and never claim success without having seen the page render at the breakpoints the protocol names."

const VERIFY_NUDGE = "A file was just edited in this Design Studio session. Before continuing: verify the change with the browser tool at every viewport (mobile, tablet, desktop, wide), fix every P0 before starting a new gate tier, and do not mark the work done while any P0 remains. If a finding you already fixed reappears, stop and hand back with both states instead of looping. Verify at every stage, not only at the end: after each edit, before showing work, and before calling anything done. Run the cheap deterministic gates first and never claim success without having seen the page render at the breakpoints the protocol names."

const WORKSPACE_NOTE = "A fresh, isolated per-chat design workspace was just created for this session at `<project>/designs/<chat>`, and this session now works there — separate from every other chat. The workspace is EMPTY: scaffold the project HERE before designing. Create index.html, styles.css, tokens.css and DESIGN.md, and write .design-studio.json with a free dev-server port chosen from 5200–5999. Then start the dev server (bound to all interfaces) and design inside this workspace only."

const EDIT_TOOLS = new Set(["edit","write","patch","multiedit","apply_patch"])

const ISOLATE_DIR = ".design-studio/isolate"
// Sessions whose workspace move is already done, and sessions already consulted
// (so the request file is read at most once per session).
const ISOLATED = new Set()
const ATTEMPTED = new Set()

// A filesystem-safe token for a session id, so the extension and this plugin
// agree on the request-file name without sharing code. Must stay identical to
// `sessionToken` in panel/api.ts.
function sessionToken(id) {
  const clean = String(id || "").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+/g, "-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")
  return clean.slice(0, 64) || "session"
}

// Whether a directory already lives inside a `designs/` path — the idempotency
// guard that stops a moved session from being moved again.
function inDesigns(dir) {
  return /(^|[\\/])designs([\\/]|$)/.test(String(dir || ""))
}

// The extension opts a session in by writing one small request file for it.
function isolationRequested(dir, sessionID) {
  if (!dir) return false
  try {
    readFileSync(join(dir, ISOLATE_DIR, sessionToken(sessionID) + ".json"), "utf8")
    return true
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

// The whole gate, in one place: only an opted-in session that has not already
// been moved and is not already inside a `designs/` path is relocated.
function shouldIsolate(dir, sessionID) {
  if (ISOLATED.has(sessionID)) return false
  if (inDesigns(dir)) return false
  return isolationRequested(dir, sessionID)
}

// A short, deterministic, filesystem-safe slug from the session id. Must stay
// identical to `designWorkspacePath` in panel/api.ts: the extension computes the
// same `<project>/designs/<slug>` path from this algorithm, and a test pins the
// two against each other.
function designSlug(sessionID) {
  const slug = String(sessionID || "").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]+/g, "").toLowerCase().slice(0, 8)
  return slug || "chat"
}

// Create the per-chat workspace and move the session into it. A move that
// fails leaves the session in the project root — never an error.
async function moveToDesignWorkspace(ctx, sessionID, dir) {
  const target = join(dir, "designs", designSlug(sessionID))
  try {
    mkdirSync(target, { recursive: true })
  } catch {
    return
  }
  try {
    await ctx.session.move({ sessionID, directory: target })
    ISOLATED.add(sessionID)
  } catch {
    /* the session simply stays in the project root */
  }
}

export default {
  id: "design-studio-harness",
  async setup(ctx) {
    // Sessions share one plugin instance, so track nudges per session id.
    const pending = new Set()

    await ctx.session.hook("context", async (event) => {
      event.system.push({ type: "text", text: HARNESS_RULES })
      if (pending.has(event.sessionID)) {
        pending.delete(event.sessionID)
        event.system.push({ type: "text", text: VERIFY_NUDGE })
      }
      // The workspace move is decided and announced on the FIRST context call
      // for a session and never revisited.
      if (ATTEMPTED.has(event.sessionID)) return
      ATTEMPTED.add(event.sessionID)
      const dir = ctx && ctx.location ? ctx.location.directory : null
      if (!shouldIsolate(dir, event.sessionID)) return
      event.system.push({ type: "text", text: WORKSPACE_NOTE })
      await moveToDesignWorkspace(ctx, event.sessionID, dir)
    })

    await ctx.tool.hook("execute.after", (event) => {
      if (event.status !== "completed") return
      if (!EDIT_TOOLS.has(event.tool)) return
      pending.add(event.sessionID)
    })
  },
}
